title: A Confession for the Autopsy
premise: When the coffin of Ashford Vale's founder, Edmund Hale, is exhumed for a centennial ceremony, Wren Marchetti—the night dispatcher who hears the town's secrets through his headset—realizes he once took a call from someone claiming to be inside the Hale mausoleum. The empty coffin forces him to admit the voice was real: a witness to a murder everyone believes died twenty-five years ago. As Wren follows dispatch logs and buried confessions toward the truth of who Hale really was—and who killed to protect the town's founding myth—he must choose between exposing the powerful families who built their legacy on the lie and protecting Ada, the woman hiding in plain sight as the anniversary dinner approaches. In the end, Wren broadcasts the confession over the taxi company's radio band during the dinner toast, forcing the town to hear what it paid for its survival.
about_author: Sebastian Kavanagh spent seven years answering phones at a small-town cab depot before turning to fiction, a job he credits for teaching him that every call carries a second story underneath. He writes mysteries from a rented room above a shuttered garage, where he still keeps an old radio scanner running out of habit.

chapters.title: The Grave That Answered
chapters.summary: Wren Marchetti, night-shift dispatcher, listens in on police chatter as workers open founder Edmund Hale's coffin and find it empty. His hands shake because he recognizes something no one else does. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional detachment—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Static and Second Voices
chapters.summary: Wren digs out old dispatch tapes and finds a call logged twenty-five years ago: a woman's whisper saying she saw what happened in the Hale house, then silence. His supervisor orders him to hand over the tape. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve; he kept the copy out of cowardice, now it's evidence.

chapters.title: A Town Built on Toasts
chapters.summary: Wren walks the daylight streets he usually avoids, watching the town prepare its centennial anniversary dinner while the mayor spins the empty coffin as vandalism. Everyone performs grief for a man whose body they never saw. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: alienation sharpening into suspicion of collective complicity.

chapters.title: Fares Who Talk Too Much
chapters.summary: Through driver radio chatter, Wren maps who visited the cemetery overnight—including councilwoman Vivian Ashe, whose family name appears beside Hale's on every founding document. POV: Wren, with interlaced driver transmissions. Emotional beat: the thrill of seeing power's choreography from below.

chapters.title: The Woman in Seat Nine
chapters.summary: Reviewing cab records, Wren realizes 'Ada Lindqvist,' a quiet regular, matches the age and neighborhood of the missing witness, Lena Voss, presumed dead since 1999. He says nothing—but starts routing her rides himself. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: tenderness arriving uninvited, duty and desire beginning to pull apart.

chapters.title: What the Mausoleum Kept
chapters.summary: Wren breaks into the Hale mausoleum at 3 a.m. and finds the crypt hollowed into a living space—canned food, a cot, decades-old newspapers. Someone lived here until recently. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: vertigo; the town's sacred monument was a hiding place all along.

chapters.title: Vivian's Version
chapters.summary: Vivian Ashe summons Wren, offering him a promotion and a warning: the Voss woman was unstable, the family closed this chapter long ago, and dispatchers who dig become liabilities. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: seduction and threat braided together; he understands the price of survival is obedience.

chapters.title: Ada, Off the Record
chapters.summary: Wren drives Ada home himself. She knows he knows. Over coffee she admits only fragments: she changed her name, she trusts no institution, and the man in the mausoleum was her brother, keeping watch until it was safe. POV: alternating Wren and Ada. Emotional beat: two invisible people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Brother's Last Log
chapters.summary: Ada gives Wren her brother Tomas's notebook: twenty-five years of observations proving Edmund Hale was murdered by his own partners, and that Lena Voss witnessed it. The last entry names a date—the anniversary dinner—as when 'they'll finish it.' POV: Wren reading. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger who died guarding the truth.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Frequency
chapters.summary: Wren discovers Tomas used the taxi company's unused emergency band to communicate; old recordings survive in the basement server. Among them: a recording of the murder night itself, half-captured by a cab's dash mic. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: horror and awe—the town's own infrastructure preserved its crime.

chapters.title: Three Names on the Ledger
chapters.summary: The recording implicates not one killer but three founding families, including the Ashes. Wren confronts the arithmetic: expose them and destroy Ada's safety, or bury it and become what they are. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes—power corrupts precisely because silence is affordable to some and fatal to others.

chapters.title: Someone Is Driving My Routes
chapters.summary: A substitute driver takes Ada's usual fare and asks questions about her. Wren realizes the network is hunting her before the dinner. He falsifies dispatch records to break her pattern. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into protective action; love stops being abstract.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Mayor Corliss Hale, Edmund's grandson, meets Wren privately—not with threats but with sympathy, claiming he too suspects his grandfather's death wasn't natural, and asking for the tapes 'to do it right.' POV: Wren. Emotional beat: doubt as a weapon; Wren can't tell ally from angler.

chapters.title: Burn the Basement
chapters.summary: The dispatch office suffers a small fire; the archive room is destroyed. Wren survives scrutiny only because he'd moved the recordings home days earlier—a precaution born of paranoia he can't explain even to himself. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt inverted; his instinct to hide saved the truth.

chapters.title: Ada Breaks Her Silence
chapters.summary: Ada tells Wren everything: she was fourteen, hiding in the Hale house pantry, and heard her father refuse to join the cover-up; his death was ruled an accident. She stayed silent to live. Now Tomas's death has ended her patience. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: catharsis; the cost of survival named aloud at last.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Security sweeps the town, guest lists tighten, and Wren learns the dinner toast will include the reburial of a symbolic casket—giving the conspirators a final ritual closure and a crowd of witnesses. Whatever happens must happen there. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: claustrophobic anticipation; the trap and the stage are the same room.

chapters.title: The Longest Shift
chapters.summary: Wren works the dinner night as official transport coordinator, moving between ballroom and cabstand, passing the tapes' contents to a retired journalist among the guests while dodging Vivian's watchful aide. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: controlled terror; the invisible man learning to move in light.

chapters.title: Glass Raised, Truth Broadcast
chapters.summary: As the mayor lifts his glass, Wren hijacks the venue's PA via the taxi radio band and plays the murder-night recording, then Ada walks in alive. The room shatters; Vivian moves to cut the power; the journalist's recorder runs. POV: Wren and Ada. Emotional beat: climax—love against duty resolved as both, together, choosing exposure.

chapters.title: What Power Does When Cornered
chapters.summary: In the chaos, Corliss reveals he engineered the exhumation himself, unable to live on the lie—but Vivian's faction attempts to flee with the ledger. A chase through the kitchen corridors ends with the state troopers Wren quietly summoned holding the doors. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fury and release; corruption exposed cannot negotiate.

chapters.title: Testimony at Dawn
chapters.summary: Ada gives her formal statement; Wren surrenders the tapes and accepts he'll lose his job for the illegal broadcast. The town wakes to headlines naming three families. Some neighbors thank him; others spit. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the lonely aftermath of doing right; visibility hurts exactly as much as feared.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Edmund Hale's actual remains—recovered from the riverbed where Tomas's notes said they'd be—are laid to rest properly, with Ada attending under her own true name, Lena Voss. Tomas is honored beside her father. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: mourning finally permitted; the dead given back their names.

chapters.title: Night Shift, New Voice
chapters.summary: Months later, Wren trains a new dispatcher, teaching her to hear the second story under every call. Ada waits outside with two coffees. The scanner still murmurs, but the frequency feels different now—watched over, not haunted. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; survival repurposed into guardianship, love chosen over safety.
